parakeet: Yes, it is true that we cannot prove or disprove the existence of God, and the important thing is that's not a claim we make. We don't claim to have proof. We acknowledge the lack of proof either way, and therefore the lack of good reason to believe one way or another. But we can prove or disprove causal claims attached to specific gods. For example, some people used to claim that Zeus caused thunderstorms. Those claims have been debunked, and we know that thunderstorms are the result of natural processes. Though sadly there are still quite a significant number of Christians who still believe that their God uses storms to punish the wicked. And we can also prove or disprove the relevance of any God or the belief in any God. We can run a variety of experiments to test if your belief in a God will move your God to action in any significant way. And we can prove or disprove the utility of any God or the belief in any God because God exists outside of the natural world. God is by default irrelevant to the natural world. There you go.
